title: Revert of upstream #272 float macros to the fork's clamp/align/nearest-rounding FPU semantics
problem: The fork says SotC gameplay math matched only with its own semantics. These are: ADD/SUB drop operand bits shifted out of the aligned mantissa; DIV/SQRT switch MXCSR to round-to-nearest; results clamped to +/-FLT_MAX.
approach: Replaces ps2_fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt and ps2_vadd/vsub/vmul with ps2FpuAdd/Sub (ps2FpuAlignOperands), ps2FpuClamp(a*b), ps2FpuDivideNearest, ps2FpuSqrtNearest(fabs). The VU macros become ps2VuClampVector(_mm_add_ps).
scope_evidence: Intent is general, but this is a whole-scheme swap tuned and bisected on SotC ('Bisect revert'). It drops #272's handling of exponent-255 inputs: host a+b sees them as Inf/NaN before the clamp. I verified PCSX2 FPU.cpp interpreter ADD_S does NOT align operands; alignment exists only in PCSX2's recompiler, which I did not verify this session.

title: EE FPU C.cond.S compares PS2 floats as ordered sign-magnitude values
problem: Host float compares treat exponent-255 patterns (e.g. 0x7FFFFFFF) as NaN, so EQ/LT/LE come out false and UN true. The EE has no NaN. -0 and denormals must compare equal to 0.
approach: New ps2FpuCompareKey(): denormal/zero becomes 0, then a sign-magnitude-to-unsigned ordering key. All C.cond macros compare keys. UN, NGLE and SF return 0; the U*/NG* variants alias the ordered ones.
scope_evidence: General. The test comment mentions SotC's horse steering sentinel, but the code has no title logic. It fits #272's extended-range semantics. Slight difference from the PCSX2 interpreter: PCSX2 fpuDouble clamps exponent 255 to 0x7F7FFFFF, so PCSX2 treats 0x7FFFFFFF == 0x7F7FFFFF; the key scheme orders them.
upstream_equivalent: #321 'order PS2 floats as sign-magnitude for compares, MIN/MAX and VU MAX/MINI' (broader)

title: VU0 R register (VRNEXT/VRINIT/VRXOR/VRGET/CTC2 R), VFTOI saturation, VABS denormal flush, shared R across contexts
problem: VRNEXT used an invented LFSR and never wrote Ft. VRINIT/VRXOR used invented mixing. CTC2 R did not force 0x3F800000|mantissa. VFTOI did not saturate positive overflow (cvttps gives 0x80000000). VABS kept denormals. Each thread had its own R.
approach: VRNEXT: r=((r<<1)^bit4^bit22)&0x7FFFFF|0x3F800000, written to Ft by the dest mask. VRINIT and VRXOR as in PCSX2. VFTOI XORs a positive-overflow mask. vf0 writes skipped. EeScheduler load/saveSharedVu0Random around each guest run.
scope_evidence: General. One deviation from PCSX2: the fork's VRNEXT advances R even when ft==0, while PCSX2 _vuRNEXT returns early without advancing.
upstream_equivalent: #318 (VFTOI saturation), #383 (VFTOI). No PR found for VRNEXT/LFSR.

title: dispatchGuestBranch: a checkpoint unwind or recursive tail jump is not an implicit return
problem: After targetFn returns, `if (ctx->pc == entryPc) ctx->pc = fallthroughPc` treated the callee as having returned. Two cases trigger it falsely. (a) A scheduler checkpoint unwind in recursive code leaves pc == entry, which lost frames. (b) A guest tail jump back to the callee's entry (e.g. execSCRBaseFunc -> j execSCRBaseFunc) does the same. The caller then resumed with the callee's sp and corrupted a saved ra.
approach: (a) EeScheduler gets m_unwinding, set wherever checkpointDue returns true and cleared before each run(). dispatchGuestBranch returns false if unwinding(). (b) A thread_local g_guestJumpSerial increments on every non-call dispatch. The heuristic applies only if the serial did not change during the callee. 7e6dfd97 also adds the PS2X_BRANCH_TRACE ring and PS2X_DUMP_RAM_ON_MISSING diagnostics.
scope_evidence: General control-flow correctness for recursive or tail-jumping guest code. The function names are only examples.
upstream_equivalent: #270 'unwind all callers when guest code yields to the EE scheduler' (related); #323 (related)

title: Deliver every EE timer overflow/compare event (per-timer backlog)
problem: Several overflows in one batch of elapsed cycles raised a single interrupt. Events while OVFF/EQUF were still set were dropped. SotC counts timer-0 overflows as a clock and ran at 0.89x.
approach: A global map keyed by the PS2Memory pointer holds backlog counts per timer (cap 2^20). Missed events are re-raised each time the guest clears the flag via a MODE write. Interrupts found during timer register reads are kept in 'undelivered' and the event budget is forced to 0.
scope_evidence: Semi-general. It compensates for coarse batched timer evaluation; on hardware an event while the flag is set is not queued, so this deliberately deviates when the guest acks late. The global mutex-guarded unordered_map keyed by this pointer is a design smell.

evidence.analysis: read-only source inspection by a forensic pass (2026-10-23); not built or tested here

title: GS CSR bits 0-4 write-1-to-clear, VSINT at VBlank start, INTC 0 raised for unmasked GS events
problem: Only SIGNAL/FINISH were W1C. HSINT/VSINT/EDWINT were never set or cleared, and the GS interrupt (INTC 0) was never raised.
approach: kW1cMask 0x3 becomes 0x1F in writeCsrHalf/writeCsrFull. VBlankStart does csr|=0x8. pendingGsInterruptEvents() = csr & ~(IMR>>8) & 0x1F, latched with m_gsInterruptLatched. dispatchIrq(false,0) on newly raised bits from processPendingEvents. accountCycles sets a checkpoint when pending differs from the latch.

title: VIF1 DIRECT continues a pending GIF IMAGE only from the next DIRECT payload
problem: At the top of the VIFcode loop, a pending PATH2 IMAGE consumed the following raw VIF codes as pixels. That desynchronised the stream and lost texture uploads split across DIRECT 1 + DIRECT n.
approach: The pending-image block is removed from the loop head. Inside DIRECT/DIRECTHL, the first min(pending, qwCount) qwords go out as an IMAGE packet and the rest are submitted and parsed for new pending image QWC.

title: GS alpha blend honours COLCLAMP (wrap when CLAMP=0)
problem: The blend always saturated. With COLCLAMP.CLAMP=0 hardware keeps the low 8 bits, which games use for shadow-volume tricks (SotC hull artifacts).
approach: Blend result r/g/b becomes colclamp&1 ? clampU8(x) : (x & 0xFF). Applied in gs_cpu_backend.cpp and gs_cpu_raster_inline.h (the fork's new raster).

title: Recompiler options: runtime_relocations CSV (j26/hi16/lo16 read from live guest words), constant-prop invalidation at those sites, auto_stub_by_name, direct_tail_calls
problem: Games that link code modules at runtime patch immediates and jump targets after boot. Baked link-time values or constant-propagated addresses go stale. Name-based auto stubs and direct J tail calls bypass replaceFunction().
approach: Sentinel substitution replaces the immediate with FAST_READ32(addr)&0xFFFF (signed/unsigned). J/JAL at listed sites decode the target from the live word and dispatch through the runtime. updateConstantRegisters invalidates rt for listed lui/addiu/ori, via a file-scope global pointer. Config flags all default to existing behaviour.
scope_evidence: General opt-in mechanism, but the relocation CSV is per-game data (SotC's loader). Defaults keep current behaviour.
upstream_equivalent: #348 'follow J/JAL the guest rewrites at dispatched sites' (related)
